rv.q: But while the play’s good bones are still plainly visible, this staging fails to dress them in the style that they deserve.
Although Nottage creates a satisfying tragic structure as the pieces converge in a more gripping second half, it’s effortful to get there.
Arguably carried more by the talent of actors as opposed to direction, Sweat is a must-see performance with timeless relevance.

cn.t: Nottage's Pulitzer-winning drama about American deindustrialization remains urgently relevant, but critics find this production lacks the necessary fire, with direction that doesn't fully match the power of the writing.
